title: Fix potential vulnerability in comment body interpolation
description:
We got a report about a vulnerability in this part of the CLA assistant code (see https://positpbc.atlassian.net/browse/SECEXT-1278 and https://positpbc.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1947):

```
          cat << "${{ steps.random_delimiter.outputs.value }}" | sed '/^[[:space:]]*$/d; s/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//' >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
          ${{ steps.random_delimiter.outputs.value }}
```

The concern is that `github.event.comment.body` might contain arbitrary shell code, including code that could be expanded by the shell.

However as I now better understand the code in question, I don't think there's actually a vulnerability. The heredoc delimiter is quoted in "", which prevents expansions: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/V3_chap02.html#tag_18_07_04:

> If any part of word is quoted, the delimiter shall be formed by performing quote removal on word, and the here-document lines shall not be expanded. Otherwise, the delimiter shall be the word itself. If no part of word is quoted, all lines of the here-document shall be expanded for parameter expansion, command substitution, and arithmetic expansion.

So I think the code is currently technically safe.

However it would be easy to introduce a vulnerability when changing the code by omitting the quotes around the delimiter of the heredoc. And Github recommends avoiding this sort of expansion in shell code as a general principle: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#use-an-intermediate-environment-variable. So we could apply the fix anyway (I wrote it before realising the code is actually safe). It makes the code simpler and easier to reason about or audit.
